title: Recamán's sequence at high altitude
description:
Recamán's sequence starts at 0, and its nth step subtracts n if the result is non-negative and new, and adds n otherwise. The only published upper bound on its growth appears to be the trivial a(n) ≤ n(n+1)/2. We show that, far above the values it has visited, the sequence follows a rule with no arithmetic in it: a ±1 walk steps up exactly when some earlier stretch of it has a prescribed mean. This reduces the growth question to a game on ±1 walks. A one-page argument then gives limsup a(n)/n² ≤ 3/26, and a small verified search gives 1/14.

We then study the game itself. If its reach rate is positive, optimal plays converge to stationary walks that obey the rule at every step, with no opponent. Every inequality W ≤ cD, where W counts the up-steps of a ±1 word that satisfy the rule's condition and D counts its down-steps, gives limsup a(n)/n² ≤ (c−1)/(2c+2). We prove it for c = 2. The case c = 1, which we state as a conjecture, would give a(n) = o(n²), and we show that this is equivalent to subtractions having frequency 1/2. We also describe the natural approaches to the conjecture that fail, with the words that refute them. The bounds on the sequence, the reduction to the game and the consequences of W ≤ cD are formalized in Lean 4, in about 1200 lines.

The archive contains the paper (paper/recaman.pdf, CC BY 4.0), the Lean formalization and the checking programs (Apache-2.0).
